natural_language: The period of a simple pendulum is proportional to the square root of its length divided by the local gravitational acceleration, with a dimensionless constant of proportionality of about 6.2831853. Length has the dimension of length; gravitational acceleration has length over time squared. State the dimension of the period. Note that this requires a rational, non-integer exponent.

expected_semantics.requires: rational exponent 1/2 applied to a dimension vector

distractors: Forgetting the square root and reporting Time^2.
Treating the constant 6.2831853 as carrying a dimension.
Assuming half-integer exponents cannot be checked exactly. They can, if exponents are rationals rather than floats; a float representation would make Time^0.5 squared fail to equal Time exactly.
